title: Data Intelligence: Mathematical Models, Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery
authors: Sangishetti Rajeshwari, Surneni Sushmitha, Terala Ravali, Katkuri Ravali, Mahesh Kedari.
abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies has transformed data from a supporting resource into one of the most valuable assets for modern organizations, scientific research, engineering, healthcare, business, and society. Every digital interaction generates data, while advances in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, machine learning, distributed systems, and emerging computational technologies have created unprecedented opportunities to transform this data into meaningful knowledge and actionable intelligence. However, the ability to collect large volumes of data alone does not guarantee meaningful outcomes. Effective data intelligence requires a strong foundation in mathematical modelling, statistical reasoning, data engineering, machine learning, analytical discovery, responsible artificial intelligence, and intelligent decision-making. With this perspective, we have developed Data Intelligence: Mathematical Models, Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery as a comprehensive academic textbook for students, educators, researchers, and professionals seeking to understand the principles and applications of modern data intelligence. The book is designed to establish a progressive learning pathway, beginning with mathematical and statistical foundations, moving through data engineering and machine learning, advancing toward modern analytical intelligence and generative AI, and concluding with practical case studies, responsible AI, and future directions. The central objective of this book is to bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and practical analytical applications. Mathematics provides the language through which data relationships can be represented and analysed, statistics provides the principles for reasoning under uncertainty, data engineering provides the infrastructure for preparing and managing information, and machine learning provides computational methods for discovering patterns and making predictions. Modern developments such as generative AI, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multimodal intelligence, AI agents, federated learning, quantum machine learning, digital twins, and autonomous analytics further extend the possibilities of data-driven intelligence. The book therefore approaches data intelligence as an integrated discipline rather than as a collection of isolated technologies. Chapter 1, Foundations of Data Intelligence and Mathematical Models, establishes the conceptual and mathematical foundation of the subject. It begins with the evolution, concepts, and scope of data intelligence and examines how data ecosystems, data sources, data lifecycles, and data-driven decision-making contribute to intelligent organizations. The chapter introduces vectors, matrices, tensors, and linear algebra, followed by probability, statistics, and statistical inference. Correlation, covariance, regression, statistical models, optimization, gradient methods, and mathematical modelling are subsequently discussed. The chapter also emphasizes data quality, data governance, data management, privacy, ethics, and responsible data intelligence, providing an essential foundation for the chapters that follow. Chapter 2, Data Engineering, Analytics and Machine Learning, focuses on the transformation of raw data into analytical information and machine learning knowledge. Data collection, integration, cleaning, and transformation are presented as essential components of reliable analytical systems. Exploratory data analysis and analytical visualization are introduced to help learners understand patterns, distributions, relationships, and trends within datasets. The chapter then develops important machine learning concepts including feature engineering, dimensionality reduction, supervised learning, regression, classification, decision trees, ensemble learning, support vector machines, clustering, association rule mining, recommendation systems, and customer analytics. Particular attention is given to model training, validation, evaluation, and optimization so that learners understand not only how models are developed but also how their performance and reliability are assessed. Chapter 3, Advanced Machine Learning and Analytical Discovery, moves from foundational machine learning toward advanced computational intelligence. Neural networks and deep learning architectures are introduced as powerful approaches for learning complex representations from data. Convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models are explored in relation to visual data, sequential information, language, and other complex analytical tasks. Time-series forecasting and predictive intelligence demonstrate how historical observations can support future-oriented analysis. The chapter further addresses anomaly, fraud, and risk detection, followed by explainable and interpretable machine learning. Causal AI and causal discovery introduce methods for understanding cause-and-effect relationships rather than relying exclusively on statistical associations. Prescriptive analytics, decision intelligence, automated machine learning, and intelligent analytical discovery complete the chapter by demonstrating how analytical systems can progress from prediction toward recommendations and automated knowledge discovery. Chapter 4, Generative AI, Emerging Technologies and Applications, examines the rapidly evolving technologies that are redefining contemporary data intelligence. Generative AI, large language models, and foundation models are presented as important components of modern intelligent systems. Retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge-based intelligence demonstrate how external knowledge can be integrated with generative models. The chapter explores multimodal intelligence, AI agents, and agentic analytics, emphasizing systems capable of processing diverse information and supporting complex analytical workflows. Real-time and streaming data intelligence, cloud and edge computing, synthetic data, vector databases, and knowledge graphs are discussed as important components of modern data platforms. Federated learning, privacy-preserving AI, quantum machine learning, digital twins, autonomous analytics, and Industry 5.0 further demonstrate the interdisciplinary evolution of data intelligence. The chapter concludes by examining advanced applications across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, energy, and smart cities. Chapter 5, Case Studies, Responsible AI and Future Directions, connects the concepts developed throughout the book with realistic application scenarios. Healthcare applications demonstrate disease prediction and personalized healthcare, while finance applications examine credit risk and intelligent fraud detection. Retail analytics explores customer segmentation and recommendation intelligence. Manufacturing applications focus on predictive maintenance and industrial intelligence. Smart city and energy applications demonstrate traffic and energy demand forecasting, while cybersecurity applications address intelligent anomaly and intrusion detection. A dedicated generative AI case study examines enterprise knowledge discovery using large language models and retrieval-augmented generation. The final section considers the future of data intelligence through responsible AI, autonomous analytics, and AI-native data platforms. A distinguishing feature of this book is its emphasis on the relationship between mathematical foundations, computational methods, analytical reasoning, and real-world decision-making. Learners are encouraged to understand not only what an algorithm does, but also why it works, what assumptions it makes, how its performance should be evaluated, and where it can be applied responsibly. Mathematical and statistical concepts are therefore connected with machine learning and analytical applications throughout the book. This approach is intended to support both conceptual understanding and practical problem-solving. We have also given considerable importance to the principles of responsible data intelligence. The increasing deployment of AI systems creates important questions concerning privacy, security, fairness, transparency, accountability, interpretability, governance, and human oversight. Data-driven systems can influence healthcare decisions, financial services, industrial operations, public infrastructure, and individual experiences. Consequently, technical capability must be accompanied by responsible design and appropriate governance. The book treats responsible AI not as an independent topic but as a continuing consideration across the data intelligence lifecycle. The book is intended to serve a broad academic audience. Undergraduate and postgraduate students in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Engineering, and related disciplines can use it as a textbook or supplementary reference. Faculty members may use the structured chapters and applications for classroom teaching, laboratory discussions, seminars, project guidance, and curriculum development. Researchers and practitioners may also find the book useful as a foundation for exploring advanced topics and interdisciplinary applications of data intelligence. The organization of the book is deliberately progressive. Readers first develop an understanding of data, mathematics, statistics, modelling, governance, and ethics. They then progress toward data engineering, machine learning, advanced analytical methods, generative AI, emerging technologies, and application-oriented case studies. This progression is intended to make the subject accessible to learners while retaining sufficient technical depth for advanced academic study. We acknowledge that data intelligence is an evolving field. New algorithms, architectures, platforms, models, and applications continue to emerge at a remarkable pace. title: 基于自适应的动态概率场优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability field optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance of machine learning models, particularly in scenarios with sparse data. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on fixed, pre-defined parameters, limiting their adaptability. We introduce a dynamically adjustable probability field, which allows the algorithm to learn and optimize the model's parameters in real-time, adapting to varying data characteristics. The core mechanism leverages the inherent self-adaptability of machine learning models to dynamically adjust the probability field, leading to improved prediction accuracy. We provide a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, a comparison with existing methods, and illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness on a dataset focused on sparse data scenarios.

title: 基于高维非线性图的自适应学习框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning framework based on high-dimensional non-linear graphs. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual feature engineering, limiting the model's ability to effectively handle complex data distributions. This framework leverages the inherent complexity of high-dimensional non-linear graphs to automatically adjust parameters, enabling automatic data preprocessing and feature extraction. The core mechanism centers around an adaptive learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts the graph's structure to better represent the data's underlying patterns. The design incorporates a novel graph representation and a sophisticated optimization strategy, resulting in improved performance on a diverse set of datasets. The results demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in automatically identifying and extracting crucial features, significantly enhancing data quality and model accuracy.

title: Cognitive Architecture Evolved by Evolutionary Algorithms (CAEA)
abstract: This paper proposes the Cognitive Architecture Evolved by Evolutionary Algorithms (CAEA) framework, a novel approach to designing and optimizing cognitive architectures using evolutionary algorithms. The core claim is that the adaptive evolution of cognitive architectures can be facilitated by leveraging the principles of evolutionary computation. The central mechanism involves treating a cognitive architecture as a population, employing genetic algorithms to drive its evolution, and utilizing selection, crossover, and mutation operators to refine architectural parameters and structure. CAEA represents a significant departure from traditional cognitive architecture design methods by introducing an automated, self-organizing optimization process. The paper details the key components of the CAEA framework, including the representation of cognitive architectures as genetic individuals, the implementation of evolutionary operators, and the evaluation metrics for assessing architectural performance. We demonstrate the potential of CAEA to create more robust and adaptable cognitive systems, particularly in complex and dynamic environments. The framework's ability to automatically explore a vast design space offers a promising avenue for developing truly intelligent systems.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Variables
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal Bayesian network modeling that explicitly incorporates latent variables. Traditional causal Bayesian networks often struggle to represent complex systems where causal relationships are obscured by unobserved factors. We propose a framework for learning causal structure within Bayesian networks, specifically designed to identify and model these mediating latent variables. The core claim is that accurate modeling necessitates representing unobserved causal relationships. The central mechanism involves an algorithm capable of discovering and integrating latent variables into the network structure. This addresses shortcomings in existing methods and provides a more realistic representation of systems with hidden influences. The developed framework offers a significant advancement in causal inference techniques, paving the way for improved understanding and prediction in diverse domains.

title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Emergent Communication Protocols
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of cooperative multi-agent systems, specifically addressing the challenges associated with designing explicit communication protocols. We propose a novel approach utilizing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to enable agents to learn emergent communication protocols autonomously. Our system allows agents to coordinate their actions effectively without pre-defined rules, fostering a truly emergent form of communication. The core of our method lies in the agents' ability to discover optimal communication strategies through trial and error, guided by a reward function that incentivizes cooperative behavior. We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and leverage deep neural networks to approximate the value function and policy. The emergent protocols are not programmed but arise from the learning process itself, demonstrating a significant advancement over traditional communication-based approaches. This research contributes to the field of multi-agent systems by providing a framework for creating adaptive, robust, and intelligent communication strategies in complex environments. The key performance indicator is the efficiency of task completion as measured by the average task success rate. The system is evaluated across a range of scenarios, showcasing the effectiveness of the emergent communication protocols in achieving superior cooperative performance.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Feature Extraction and Representation Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to feature extraction and representation learning within the context of quantum machine learning. The core claim is to enhance the performance and efficiency of machine learning algorithms by leveraging quantum computation for these foundational tasks. We introduce a methodology that utilizes quantum algorithms to transform raw data into representations optimized for subsequent machine learning processes. This represents a new direction in the burgeoning field of quantum machine learning, offering potential advantages over classical methods, particularly for complex datasets and computationally intensive tasks. The paper details the theoretical framework, outlines the key components of the proposed system, and discusses potential applications and future research directions. The primary focus is on the algorithmic design and mathematical foundations underpinning this approach, aiming to provide a solid basis for future development and experimentation.

title: Quantum State Geometry Mapping
abstract: Quantum State Geometry Mapping (QSGM) is a novel approach to quantum state representation and computation, aiming to translate complex quantum states into geometric spaces. This paper introduces a method leveraging geometric optimization to enhance the processing and analysis of high-dimensional quantum states. The core principle is to map a quantum state to a geometric structure, allowing for efficient calculation and analysis through geometric optimization techniques. We present a framework for mapping quantum states to higher-dimensional geometric spaces, demonstrating its potential to improve computational efficiency and provide new insights into quantum systems. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithms and offers a unique perspective on the representation and manipulation of quantum states.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architecture for a Physical Simulation Engine of Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to simulating neural networks by employing a physical simulation engine. Instead of relying on traditional mathematical models, we represent neurons and synapses as physical particles governed by Newtonian mechanics. The interactions between these particles, primarily through forces dictated by synaptic strengths, simulate the transmission of signals and the dynamic behavior of neural networks. This methodology offers a potentially more scalable and robust approach to modeling complex neural network phenomena, particularly those involving intricate spatial arrangements and emergent behaviors. The core of this engine is the accurate representation of synaptic connections as physical forces, allowing for a more realistic and potentially more powerful simulation of biological neural networks compared to conventional methods. The simulation relies on the principle of particle interaction to mimic the complex dynamics of neuronal networks.

The core of this engine is the accurate representation of synaptic connections as physical forces, allowing for a more realistic and potentially more powerful simulation of biological neural networks compared to conventional methods. The simulation relies on the principle of particle interaction to mimic the complex dynamics of neuronal networks.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Comparative Analysis Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Self-Organizing Fractal Networks for High-Dimensional Data Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to high-dimensional data representation using Self-Organizing Fractal Networks (SOFNs). The core challenge in representing complex, high-dimensional data is the "curse of dimensionality," which significantly hinders the performance of traditional neural networks. Our proposed solution leverages fractal geometry to create a network architecture that is inherently scalable and efficient. The SOFN consists of nodes arranged in a recursive, scale-invariant fractal structure. The network learns by iteratively refining this structure based on local information, effectively capturing intricate patterns within the data. We demonstrate the potential of SOFNs to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, offering a promising direction for future research in high-dimensional data analysis. The key mathematical formulation and network structure are presented, outlining the iterative refinement process and the scale-invariant properties of the fractal network. The goal is to achieve higher accuracy and efficiency in representing complex data while minimizing the computational burden. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Dynamic System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to dynamic system modeling by integrating principles from quantum mechanics into the framework of reservoir computing. Traditional reservoir computing relies on a randomly connected network, often referred to as a 'reservoir', to capture complex temporal dynamics. However, this approach can be limited in its ability to represent highly intricate behaviors. We introduce the concept of a "quantum reservoir," where each node within the reservoir is represented as a superposition of multiple potential states, mimicking the quantum mechanical phenomenon of superposition. Furthermore, we incorporate entanglement between nodes through specifically designed non-linear activation functions, drawing inspiration from quantum entanglement. This integration aims to significantly enhance the reservoir's capacity to model dynamic systems, potentially unlocking exponentially greater modeling capabilities. We present a theoretical framework and discuss the implications of this approach, highlighting its potential benefits and challenges. The core of this work lies in the exploration of how quantum-inspired techniques can fundamentally transform the operation and effectiveness of reservoir computing.

title: Synthetic Taichi-Encoded Spatial Biphoton Models: Counterfactual Entanglement Tests, Reciprocal-Mode Compression, and a Prospective Blind Witness Protocol
abstract: A recognizable quantum image need not determine the entanglement of the bipartite state that produced it. This paper studies that distinction in a fully specified synthetic spatial-biphoton model whose pump amplitude follows a Taichi Diagram morphology. The morphology is engineered preparation data, not a spontaneous image of entanglement and not historical evidence for quantum mechanics. The analysis separates pump morphology, the signal–idler tensor partition, reference-relative phase, and the complete complex joint kernel. For a normalized pure kernel, an integrated rectangle-defect identity equals one minus the reduced-state purity; in coordinate form it is the linear-entropy or I-concurrence invariant. A displayed diagonal nevertheless fails to determine entanglement, as exact separable and maximally entangled controls show. The source-admitted finite model fixes cell-center coordinates, quadrature, exact Taichi Diagram masks, eye locations, Gaussian convention, phase maps, normalization, interventions, scan grids, and resolution grids. At the declared 18 × 18 grid per arm, the baseline has purity 0.441336, effective Schmidt number 2.265849, entropy 1.473719 nats, eye-region capacity 3.614 percent, and leading-two Schmidt weight 78.730 percent. Host continuation lowers the Schmidt number to 2.108193, whereas support excision raises it to 2.358247. A deterministic random midpoint phase leaves the complete joint intensity unchanged to numerical precision but changes the Schmidt number to 108.558946 and reduces fidelity with the zero-phase state to 0.000857. Complete joint-pixel dephasing preserves the image and both eyes while producing a separable state. Optimal Schmidt truncation requires 10 modes for 95 percent weight and 78 modes for 99 percent, yet an equal-weight two-mode projector already exceeds its separable bound; after the top-two local filter its target fidelity is 0.889270. The paper gives a leakage-aware partial-transpose test, a two-copy purity test, explicit prospective mode-sorter and Hong–Ou–Mandel or local Z/X/Y analyzer maps, and exact one-sided binomial design calculations. A deterministic 80-block mock TRAIN/CALIBRATION/HOLDOUT execution is included, but the block-resolved experimental data and code described by the motivating article were not obtained or analyzed. The central result is both positive and negative: compact calibrated measurements can witness coherence in the full synthetic kernel, while the visible Taichi Diagram eye regions neither determine the leading Schmidt subspace nor constitute an entanglement witness. The source archive also separates numerical SVD right singular vectors from physical idler Schmidt kets, verifies the distinction on non-real symmetric kernels, and states the additional unitary freedom required inside degenerate singular subspaces.

title: Federated learning for multi-institutional AI in healthcare via digital pathology
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital pathology has shown significant promise in advancing cancer diagnostics, grading, and treatment response prediction. However, widespread development and deployment of robust AI models face critical challenges due to data silos, privacy concerns, and the need for large-scale multi-institutional datasets. Federated Learning (FL) presents a transformative approach by enabling collaborative model training across hospitals without direct data sharing. In this review, we summarize recent developments in FL as applied to digital pathology, highlight pioneering use cases, and explore the technical, regulatory, and ethical hurdles. We discuss how FL can enable scalable, privacy-preserving AI models, and outline future directions for standardizing and validating FL-based approaches in clinical workflows.

title: Mesh Multi‐Context Protocol: An Adaptive Agentic AI With Mesh Concept for A Complex Ecosystem
abstract: ABSTRACT The deployment of Agentic AI systems‐autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) ‐ has exposed critical vulnerabilities in multi‐domain enterprise environments, with recent incidents including autonomous production database deletions highlighting fundamental architectural limitations. While frameworks such as the Multi‐Context Protocol (MCP) enable LLMs to access multiple data sources, they lack domain specialization, fault isolation, and federated governance mechanisms necessary for safe enterprise‐scale deployment across heterogeneous legacy systems. This paper introduces the Mesh Multi‐Context Protocol (MMP), a novel framework synthesizing Agentic AI capabilities with mesh topology principles to address these limitations. MMP contributes five key innovations: dynamic node management, domain‐specialized nodes, legacy system integration, lightweight operation and federated multi‐node topology. By treating each domain as an autonomous node, MMP enables safe cross‐organizational coordination while maintaining data sovereignty and preventing systemic failures. Unlike existing approaches requiring large foundation models and centralized orchestration, MMP supports lightweight domain‐specific language models with incremental adoption pathways suitable for air‐gapped, highly regulated environments including healthcare, government, and financial services. Through comprehensive architectural analysis, we demonstrate how MMP addresses fundamental challenges of deploying autonomous AI agents in complex ecosystems where privacy preservation, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience are paramount, establishing the theoretical foundation for empirical validation in real‐world system‐of‐systems scenarios.

title: MemoryLACE: Memory Lifecycle-Aware Consolidation and Evidence Retrieval
abstract: Long-term LLM agents must preserve information across interactions while distinguishing repeated evidence, historical states, updates, and unresolved contradictions. Existing textual memory systems retrieve semantically relevant memories efficiently but often leave these relationships implicit, whereas richer structured approaches model them through global graphs, hierarchical abstractions, or reflection at greater complexity. We introduce MemoryLACE (MemLACE), a lightweight memory framework that explicitly models the lifecycle of textual evidence through sparse merge, supersession, and contradiction relations while preserving atomic natural-language memories and their provenance. Rather than retrieving memories independently, MemLACE reconstructs relation-aware evidence units that expose current, historical, supporting, and conflicting evidence for downstream reasoning. Across BEAM and StructMemEval, using open-weight and proprietary LLM backbones, MemLACE achieves the highest overall performance in same-backbone comparisons while reducing end-to-end runtime on BEAM by 66.6% relative to Hindsight, the strongest reported reflective-memory baseline. Ablation studies identify lifecycle expansion and temporal awareness as the principal contributors to these gains. Together, the results demonstrate that explicitly modeling the local lifecycle of textual evidence is sufficient to substantially improve long-term memory reasoning without requiring comprehensive knowledge graphs or global reflection.

title: A Quantum Algorithm for the Radical of a Lie Algebra: Kernel Projection and Conditioning
abstract: Every finite-dimensional real or complex Lie algebra has a largest solvable ideal, its radical. In the compact dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) of a closed quantum system, this radical is the center; projecting onto it isolates directions that commute with the supplied algebra. With sparse Lie-bracket data and a known spectral gap, we construct a quantum circuit that approximately encodes this coefficient-space projector. The general construction combines the derived-algebra map with the Killing form, whereas compactness makes the Killing form alone sufficient. This distinction matters for numerical sensitivity, and our main theorem gives its exact law under an invariant-orthonormal basis adapted to the center and semisimple part. In a compact real algebra with a nonzero semisimple part, the condition number of the general operator is the three-halves power of the Killing-form condition number on that part. The compact projector in turn yields a bounded-error test for whether the center is trivial, provided that any nonzero center has at least a stated minimum dimension. This gives a controlled test for internal conserved directions in compact quantum dynamics.

title: A Review of Jellyfish Search Optimizer: Variants, Applications, and Developments
abstract: The Jellyfish Search Optimizer (JSO) is a population-based metaheuristic developed in 2021 by simulating the jellyfish movement in the ocean current and inside a swarm. Its simple structure, small number of parameters, and explicit time-control mechanism have facilitated its rapid adoption, but have also led to numerous variants that differ substantially in novelty and empirical validity. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of peer-reviewed JSO research published from 2023 onward, using the original algorithm and the 2022 state-of-the-art review as conceptual baselines. The review addresses the following four questions: Which components of JSO have been modified? Which problem classes were addressed? What is the evidence for its claimed advancements? What are the ongoing gaps in research? Recent variants are grouped into five categories: multi-strategy continuous variants, hybrid metaheuristics, binary and discrete formulations, machine-learning wrapper methods, and problem-embedded variants. The applications have been clustered into: the power and energy fields, PV modelling and maximum power point tracking, engineering designs, logistical services, troubleshooting diagnosis, prediction for the environment and analytics, etc. Across the reviewed studies, enhancements predominantly rely on chaotic and low-discrepancy initialization, opposition-learning methods, heavy-tailed mutation, neighborhood search, local-escape operators, and hybridization with other optimizers. The most impactful research applied latest CEC standard values, engineered problem cases, non-parametric tests, and complexity assessments. However, the most frequently reported weaknesses include unequal function-evaluation budgets, insufficient ablation studies, limited baseline sets, inadequate reporting of stochastic variability, and problem-specific experiments that do not establish generalizability.

title: Probability Logic: Deepening the Symmetry of Non-Symmetricity
abstract: The study of probability logic offers a powerful framework for understanding and manipulating uncertainty. However, the inherent nature of probability logic – particularly in its non-symmetric forms – often presents challenges for algorithmic optimization and machine learning. This paper explores a novel approach to enhanced probability logic analysis, focusing on the identification and utilization of hidden non-symmetry within probability distributions. We introduce a "Non-Symmetric Probability Window" mechanism, leveraging statistical differences between probability distributions to uncover potential non-symmetric patterns. This method is then applied to optimize decision-making processes and improve the performance of machine learning algorithms. The development of this approach promises to yield more effective solutions than traditional methods, capitalizing on the unique properties of probability logic.

title: 基于量子模型的概率推理
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize probabilistic reasoning, focusing on the development of a novel system for complex model inference and prediction. Traditional probabilistic reasoning methods are limited by computational constraints, while quantum computing offers the promise of enhanced speed and accuracy. We propose a system that leverages quantum algorithms to simulate probabilistic behavior and guide prediction, with a specific emphasis on applications in finance and bioinformatics. This work explores the core mechanism and potential benefits of utilizing quantum computation for probabilistic inference. The paper outlines the key innovations and challenges associated with this approach, ultimately aiming to demonstrate the feasibility of quantum-enhanced probabilistic reasoning.

title: Title: Self-Assembling Modular Arithmetic Systems for Cryptography
abstract: This paper explores the potential of self-assembling modular arithmetic systems as a novel approach to cryptography, aiming to enhance security and resilience. The core concept revolves around the design of a distributed key space generated through a process of module assembly based on physical properties and algorithmic manipulation. The system's inherent properties – self-organization, distributed key space, and potential for enhanced security – differentiate it from existing cryptographic methods. We outline the proposed architecture, detailing the key components and the underlying mathematical principles driving the self-assembly process. The analysis will address the challenges and opportunities associated with such a system, focusing on key security properties and practical implementation considerations. We conclude with a discussion of potential future research directions and the implications of this approach for the future of cryptography.

title: High-Order Matrix Dynamic Topology Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-order matrix dynamic topology mapping technique. Traditional matrix learning methods are typically static, limiting the ability to model complex systems dynamically. Our approach leverages a dynamic topology transformation applied to a matrix, creating a framework for complex system modeling and facilitates learning and description. The core mechanism centers around constructing a matrix learning model via transformations based on the matrix's inherent topology. This method aims to improve model generalization capabilities compared to static methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Optimization for Machine Learning Model Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning model tuning based on dynamic topology optimization. Traditional machine learning model tuning often involves manual feature engineering, limiting the model's ability to effectively capture complex data patterns. Our approach leverages dynamic topology, a mathematical concept that describes the interconnectedness of elements within a system, to automatically adjust parameters and improve model performance. We propose a system that iteratively refines the model's parameters by exploring a dynamically evolving set of parameter values, guided by the underlying topology. This framework aims to achieve robust and adaptive parameter tuning, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The core mechanism involves the application of a self-adaptive learning algorithm that continuously adjusts the model's parameters based on the observed data and the structure of the underlying topology. This adaptive process leads to improved model accuracy and generalization.

title: Quantum Self-Attention (QSA): Complex Projective Attention with Constructive and Destructive Interference
abstract: Quantum Self-Attention (QSA) is a drop-in replacement for softmax attention that lifts the real probability simplex into complex projective space CP^{n-1}. By preserving phase information, QSA enables constructive and destructive interference, native subtractive logic, and antisymmetric relational encoding—capabilities impossible for softmax. This paper presents the full mathematical derivation, production-ready PyTorch implementations, and empirical benchmarks including:- 99.83% accuracy on harmonic interference (vs 97.80% softmax)- Stable training on causal arithmetic where softmax crashes- First large-scale graft of QSA into a frozen 1.3B model (DeepSeek-Coder) using NecroGraft, reducing training loss from 70.4 to 2.06 The architecture is strictly more expressive than affine-softmax models (Ω(N²) separation).

abstract: ## README for CGO Paper #200 #### Details of the Artifact of the paper "COPE: Class Outlining for Partial Scalarization of Escaping Objects" at CGO 2027 are presented below: ### Expected system configuration for evaluation: 1. OS: Ubuntu 18.04 2. H/W : x86_64 / amd64 architecture and 16 GB RAM 3. Memory: Atleast 20 GB of HDD/SSD space 4. Docker: Expected to have docker installed. --- ### Initial Setup:* Download the `cope-artifact-v1.tar.gz` file the from the zenodo link [](). 1. Load docker: Load the image from the tarball downloaded ```bash docker load -i cope-artifact-final.tar.gz ``` 2. Running the docker container: ```bash docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it cope-artifact-final:v1 ```* After sucessfully running the above commands you will land up in the root directory `artifact/` --- ### Artifact Structure:Inside the Docker container, the `artifact/` directory is organized as follows: ```textartifact/├── openj9-latest/├── static-analysis/│ ├── src/│ └── soot/├── data/│ ├── dacapo/ │ └── spec-jvm/├── output/├── results/├── *.sh└── *.R``` 1. `openj9-latest/` : Contains the modified OpenJ9 VM (v0.57.0) source code, instrumented to enable specific debugging outputs such as class sizes and debug counters. The pre-built JVM binaries (compiled for `x86_64`) are located within the `build/` subdirectory.2. `static-analysis/` : Contains the custom Soot-based static analysis framework. This includes the implementation passes for constructor inlining, field-read hoisting, class outlining, and partial scalarization. It processes the raw benchmarks and outputs the transformed bytecode.3. `data/` : Contains the input classes for each benchmark in `dacapo/` and `spec-jvm/` sub-directories. The benchmark files have been pre-extracted and resolved using the poa-agent provided in [Tamiflex](https://github.com/secure-software-engineering/tamiflex).4. `output/` : An initially empty working directory used by Soot to store the transformed benchmark code. Subdirectories use specific prefixes to denote the applied optimizations: `base_` (unoptimized Soot output), `ci_` (constructor inlining only), and `ss_` (partially-scalarized output).5. `results/` : An initially empty directory where all final evaluation artifacts including raw CSV data, intermediate logs, and the generated figures and tables are saved.6. `master-static.sh` : The primary entry point for the static analysis phase. It coordinates the following helper scripts: - `run-static-analysis.sh` : Executes the Soot passes and dumps the partially-scalarized bytecode into the `output/` directory. - `calc-memory-stats.sh` : Extracts class sizes and calculates the memory reduction metrics. - `generate-fig9.R` : Parses the static output to generate the table for Figure 9.7. `master-runtime.sh` : The primary entry point for the runtime evaluation phase. It executes the transformed code using the custom JVM and coordinates the following: - `calc-gc-dacapo.sh` / `calc-time-dacapo.sh` : Collects garbage collection and execution time data for the DaCapo benchmark suite. - `calc-spec.sh` : Collects the equivalent runtime performance metrics for the SPECjvm suite. - `generate-gc-time-plots.R` : Parses the runtime CSV data to generate the boxplots for Figure 10.8. `smoke-test.sh` : An end-to-end validation script designed to verify the artifact's functionality before a full evaluation using the `fop` benchmark from DaCapo suite. It Executes 3 JVM runs per configuration (reduced from 10) to quickly generate representative data for Figures 9 and 10. * Note that the exact values in the results might differ slightly from the paper as the numbers depend on the machine and the particular run of the benchmark (JIT compilation orders are very dynamic). But the trends are expected to remain similar. --- ### Smoke Testing We provide a streamlined `smoke-test.sh` script to quickly validate the end-to-end functionality of the artifact using the `fop` benchmark from the DaCapo suite. **Estimated Time:** ~2.5 hours **Command:** ```bashbash smoke-test.sh``` **Workflow Summary:**The smoke test verifies the entire toolchain by compiling the Soot passes, running the static analysis on `fop`, gathering memory statistics, invokes the JVM three times to execute the modified bytecode , and plotting the results. **Expected Outputs:** The smoke test isolates its data generation to the `./results/` directory. *(Note: The script also generates intermediate logs and files in this folder during execution).* Upon completion, reviewers can verify the following generated files:* `figure-9.txt`: Benchmark characteristics table for `fop`.* `Fig10-a_gc-cycles.pdf`: The garbage collection cycles plot for `fop`.* `Fig10-b_overall-execution-times.pdf`: The overall execution time plot for `fop`.* `reductions-table.txt`: A summary table showing percentage reductions in GC cycles, GC time, and overall execution time. ### Note: Extracting Results from Docker Open a new terminal on your host machine (while the container is still running) and follow these steps: 1. **Find your container ID or name:** ```bash docker ps ``` 2. **Copy the specific PDF plots:** Use the `docker cp` command to copy the files to your current host directory (represented by the `.` at the end): ```bash docker cp :/artifact/results/Fig10-a_gc-cycles.pdf . docker cp :/artifact/results/Fig10-b_overall-execution-times.pdf . ``` *(Note: Replace ` ` with your actual container ID from step 1).* --- ### Claims Supported by this Artifact 1. COPE successfully achieves partial scalarization of potentially escaping objects by extracting and scalarizing their method-local fields.2. By allocating these method-local fields on the execution stack rather than the heap, the overall per-object payload size is reduced. This results in measurable decreases in total heap memory allocation across the evaluated benchmarks, as demonstrated in **Figure 9**.3. This reduction in heap allocation pressure consequently decreases the workload on the garbage collector (GC). When running the benchmarks in memory-constrained environments, this translates to a significant reduction in total GC cycles for several benchmarks, as validated in **Figure 10(a)**.4. The decrease in GC cycles directly minimizes GC overhead, yielding overall improvements in end-to-end execution time, as illustrated in **Figure 10(b)**. > **Author's Note regarding `pmd`, `xalan`, and `fop`:** In the original paper submission, there were minor reporting errors regarding the number of objects successfully scalarized by COPE (Figure 9, Column 4: `#COPEObjs`). Specifically, we underreported the yields for `pmd` and `xalan`, and inadvertently omitted the 'M' (millions) suffix for `fop` (reporting 0.028 instead of 0.028M). The artifact correctly reflects the actual performance: COPE scalarizes approximately 0.33M objects for `pmd`, 4.9M objects for `xalan`, and 0.028M objects for `fop`. Evaluators will be able to reproduce these corrected results using this artifact. **Note on Performance Variability:** Due to non-deterministic JIT and GC behavior, and system-level noise, JVM performance numbers naturally fluctuate. For the paper, we minimized this by pinning our CPU to 2.3 GHz. While reviewers will likely see different absolute values depending on their hardware, the overall trends will match our claims. To account for this variance, our full experimental methodology involved running each benchmark through its warmup phase across 10 independent JVM invocations to generate the final plots. --- ### Starting with full-evaluation: The full evaluation reproduces the complete set of data and plots across all benchmarks. It is executed in two sequential phases: #### Phase A: Static Analysis **Command:**```bash bash master-static.sh``` **Execution Steps:**1. **Static Analysis (`run-static-analysis.sh`):** Executes the Soot passes to identify scalarization opportunities. It records the number of split classes and method-local fields identified (after constructor inlining and field-read hoisting), which generates the data for **Columns 2 and 3** of Figure 9. It also dumps the transformed bytecode into the `output/` directory under three configurations for each benchmark: * `base_` (baseline Soot with no custom passes) * `ci_` (Soot with only constructor inlining) * `ss_` (the complete COPE pipeline with class splitting and static scalarization). > Expected time: 4-5 hours 2. **Memory Statistics (`calc-memory-stats.sh`):** Evaluates the resulting memory savings. Using debug counters placed at the OpenJ9 allocation sites (running at the highest JIT optimization level), it calculates the number of objects successfully scalarized by COPE that the JIT compiler missed (**Columns 4 and 5**). It then computes the total memory saved (**Columns 6 and 7**) by comparing the class payload sizes between the `base` and `ss` configurations, using custom instrumentation added to the OpenJ9 classloader. > Expected time: 4-5 hours 3. **Table Generation:** Executes an R script that merges the data from the previous two steps to generate the complete `figure-9.txt` table. > Expected time: < 2 minutes > **Total Expected Time for Phase A:** 8–10 hours --- #### Phase B: Runtime Evaluation **Command:**```bash bash master-runtime.sh``` 1. **Runtime Evaluation (`calc-gc-dacapo.sh` & `calc-time-dacapo.sh`):** Executes the transformed bytecode of all the benchmarks one by one. The JVM performs 10 runs under constrained memory environment and in each run, the benchmark is executed it's repective warmup iteration times. title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization Algorithms for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Optimization Algorithms (QIOA) represent a novel approach to optimization, drawing inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics – specifically superposition and entanglement – to enhance the exploration of solution spaces for complex systems. This paper introduces QIOA, a new algorithm designed to address challenges inherent in optimization across diverse fields, including robotics, materials science, and financial modeling. The core mechanism centers on translating complex, multi-dimensional problems into a quantum-inspired framework, enabling efficient traversal of solution spaces and facilitating the discovery of optimal configurations. We present a detailed theoretical analysis, illustrating the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental validation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of QIOA on complex system optimization, highlighting its advantages and future research directions.

title: Cognitive Graph Construction and Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper presents a novel cognitive graph construction system and a reasoning engine designed to leverage multi-modal information for enhanced knowledge discovery and reasoning. The system utilizes a graph structure to represent knowledge and employs a reasoning engine to interpret and apply this knowledge through natural language processing. The core mechanism centers around the integration of graph information with reasoning algorithms, enabling more intelligent knowledge discovery and inference. We focus on developing a system that surpasses existing approaches by integrating both graph representation and reasoning capabilities. The paper details the system's architecture, proposes a novel reasoning process, and explores its potential applications.

title: Probabilistic Programming Languages: Formal Model Verification
abstract: This paper explores the formal verification of programs written in probabilistic programming languages (PPLs). PPLs, such as Stan, Pyro, and VCG, allow developers to express probabilistic models and computations directly, making them increasingly popular in domains like machine learning, robotics, and risk analysis. However, the inherent dynamic and stochastic nature of PPLs presents significant challenges for traditional verification techniques. This work proposes a methodology for formally verifying the correctness and safety properties of programs in PPLs by translating their semantics into a formal language and employing model checking or abstract interpretation. We outline a framework that addresses the key difficulties posed by PPLs, specifically focusing on handling uncertainty and stochasticity during the verification process. The core claim of this paper is that it is possible to perform formal verification of programs built upon PPLs. The central mechanism relies on converting the semantics of PPLs into a formal representation and subsequently utilizing model checking or abstract interpretation for verification. The research contributes to establishing a foundation for reliable development and deployment of probabilistic systems. ---

title: Quantum State Resonance Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum State Resonance Algorithm (QSRA) designed for dynamic adjustment of quantum system parameters. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, evolving parameters, hindering accurate predictions and efficient execution. The QSRA leverages the unique properties of quantum state resonance to dynamically adjust parameters, resulting in improved prediction accuracy and efficiency for quantum systems. We present a detailed theoretical framework and implementation showcasing the algorithm's effectiveness across various quantum systems. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively adjusting parameters based on a feedback loop, utilizing the resonant properties to guide optimization. The proposed method offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, addressing challenges related to parameter sensitivity and optimization speed.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Graph Structural Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-supervised learning approach specifically designed to capture and model the dynamic evolution of graph structures. Current self-supervised learning techniques predominantly concentrate on generating node embeddings, often overlooking the crucial aspect of how the graph's topology changes over time. We propose a method that learns to predict future graph states given past states, thereby directly learning the underlying dynamics inherent in the network structure. The core of our approach utilizes a recurrent neural network architecture to process sequential graph states, allowing the model to capture temporal dependencies and learn complex structural evolution patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and outline its potential applications in areas such as network monitoring, anomaly detection, and predicting cascading failures in complex systems. The primary innovation lies in treating graph structure as a time-series data and applying self-supervised learning techniques to directly model these temporal dynamics. This offers a fundamentally different perspective compared to traditional node-embedding approaches.

title: Core Claim: A machine learning-based attention mechanism optimization method proposes a dynamic adjustment of attention weights based on input data features, thereby improving the efficiency and accuracy of the attention mechanism.
abstract: Attention mechanisms have revolutionized sequence processing tasks, enabling models to focus on the most important parts of an input sequence. However, traditional attention mechanisms often rely on fixed attention weights, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex relationships within the data. This paper introduces a novel machine learning-based attention mechanism optimization method that dynamically adjusts attention weights based on input data features. The proposed method leverages an adaptive mechanism to achieve this dynamic adjustment, resulting in improved efficiency and accuracy compared to static attention techniques. We present a framework for automatically tuning attention weights, minimizing computational overhead while maintaining high performance. The core idea is to establish a learned relationship between the input data and the attention weights, allowing the model to adapt its focus as needed. This approach is particularly beneficial for long sequences and complex data structures, addressing a key limitation of existing attention models. The implementation details and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in various sequence processing tasks, showcasing a significant improvement in both accuracy and computational efficiency. The adaptive nature of the mechanism offers a significant advancement in attention optimization techniques, paving the way for more robust and efficient sequence modeling.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的特征选择算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel feature selection algorithm based on adaptive machine learning. Traditional feature selection methods are often static and lack the ability to dynamically adjust the selection process based on data distribution shifts. Our algorithm leverages learned data to automatically adjust feature selection strategies, resulting in improved model performance and efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of existing techniques by offering a more robust and adaptable solution for feature selection.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Comparative Analysis Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Temporal-Structural Stress Testing and Cross-Granularity Robustness Evaluation of Graph AI for Cryptocurrency AML Detection
abstract: Cryptocurrency anti-money-laundering (AML) is typically framed as a graph-learning problem, since suspicious value flows rarely appear as isolated records. This study examines whether graph AI architectures retain an advantage over strong non-GNN baselines when evaluation is temporal, structurally explicit, and aligned with investigator triage. We answer that question using two public Bitcoin AML datasets: Elliptic, a transaction- node dataset, and Elliptic2, a subgraph-level dataset. Our comparison spans classical models, tree ensembles, graph-derived features, graph embeddings, neural baselines, and GNN variants, evaluated across AUPRC, AUROC, accuracy, precision and recall at an investigation budget, calibration, operating points, and bootstrap uncertainty. On the temporal Elliptic test period, Extra Trees achieves AUPRC 0.570 and AUROC 0.869, while GraphSAGE, the strongest standard GNN baseline, reaches AUPRC 0.311. A strict-temporal GraphSAGE variant improves to AUPRC 0.381 but still falls behind the leading tree ensemble model. The paired bootstrap difference between Extra Trees and GraphSAGE is 0.259 AUPRC, with a 95% interval of [0.222, 0.297]. On the full Elliptic2 subgraph benchmark, Random Forest achieves AUPRC 0.494 and AUROC 0.923 in the main split and remains the strongest model by mean AUPRC across repeated splits. These findings indicate that graph AI for cryptocurrency AML should be stress-tested against capable tree ensemble models and operational metrics before architectural complexity is treated as deployment evidence.

title: Combination and access of quantum communication and 5G network
abstract: Quantum secure direct communication (QSDC), a vital branch of quantum communication, enables reliable, secure transmission under harsh conditions of high channel noise, large optical loss and stringent security constraints. Having undergone field trials and practical deployment, QSDC serves as a promising candidate for confidential transmission in ultra-high-security scenarios. Modern society relies heavily on ubiquitous communication, and 5G mobile networks have achieved rapid development and widespread commercialization in recent years, driving growing demands for robust 5G security. This paper proposes a QSDC-5G integrated secure transmission architecture to safeguard 5G data delivery. The solution maintains full compatibility with legacy classical networks while satisfying long-term security requirements for future communications. Laboratory simulation and stability tests were conducted on the proposed converged security network. Continuous 24-hour measurements demonstrate that the integrated network achieves an interface throughput of 12 kbps with a round-trip latency below 3500 ms. These key metrics satisfy the signaling transmission demands for single mobile terminal authentication when accessing private networks via base stations, laying a solid foundation for deep integration of QSDC into 5G systems.

title: Exemplar: Classical Priors Complement Frozen Features for Few-Shot Microscopy Segmentation at Native Resolution
abstract: Segmenting a new biomedical dataset usually means a domain-specific model trained on substantial annotation, or a foundation model steered at inference time. We present Exemplar, a few-shot segmenter that fuses a frozen DINOv3 backbone with a fixed bank of classical native-resolution filter responses in one lightweight head, fitted from the support masks alone. In the few-mask, native-resolution regime, classical priors and frozen self-supervised features are complementary: fused in one head, a single fixed configuration spans eleven biomedical imaging datasets. Under the same head, the classical bank alone reaches 0.693 on the eleven-dataset panel, scored by foreground intersection-over-union or centreline Dice, and the frozen features alone 0.672; the bank leads on seven of the eleven and the features on the rest, and fused they reach 0.782. Against five forward-pass few-shot methods, Exemplar leads in 54 of 55 method-dataset comparisons, 52 of them significant after Holm correction. From a single annotated mask it reaches 0.703 on the same panel, against 0.682 for a from-scratch nnU-Net trained on that same mask. At eight masks nnU-Net overtakes it on the panel mean, chiefly on centreline agreement, but takes 16-77x longer to fit.

title: Choosing a PEFT Variant for Per-Patient Dysarthric ASR: A Single-Speaker Case Study on Two ASR Bases
abstract: Per-patient adapters are the preferred production architecture for dysarthric automatic speech recognition (ASR), yet parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) variants have not been compared in the speaker-dependent, per-patient regime. We present a single-speaker case study comparing seven LoRA-family methods (LoRA, QLoRA, AdaLoRA, DoRA, LoHA, VeRA, VB-LoRA) on two production bases (Whisper-large-v3 with Hungarian fine-tuning, and a multilingual Qwen3-ASR-1.7B checkpoint) for one post-stroke Hungarian male speaker (S1, 409 utterances; severe dysarthria on auditory-perceptual clinical assessment). Attention-projection adapters substantially improve CER on both bases. Across three seeds, a paired bootstrap detects no significant LoRA-DoRA difference (p>0.5; 13.86/13.90 % CER on Whisper, 28.10/28.33 % on Qwen3-ASR), so we adopt the simpler, cheaper LoRA. Real 4-bit (NF4) QLoRA is worse on every seed and both bases (14.56/30.09 % CER) with no memory saving at this scale, and LoHA, VeRA, VB-LoRA and AdaLoRA do not reach the LoRA family, though LoHA still gives an 18.6 % relative CER reduction on Whisper. On the same base, full fine-tuning is more accurate (11.43 % CER), but a 115 MB LoRA that also adapts the feed-forward blocks reaches within 0.66 pp of it at approximately 3.7 % of the per-patient storage. A 6-point enrollment grid shows about 5 min of patient audio captures 45.6 % of the zero-shot-to-30-min CER reduction, with further gains at 10 and 30 min (caveat: one speaker, one language, severe post-stroke dysarthria). Training scripts and recipes will be released, source-available under a research-use licence, on publication.

title: PolERo: Studying Political Evasion in Romanian
abstract: Political evasion refers to responses that engage with a question while withholding the requested information. Recent NLP work frames political evasion as a classification task using a two-level taxonomy of response clarity and fine-grained evasion strategies. Existing work on response clarity and evasion classification is limited to English, leaving open whether the taxonomy and model behavior transfer across languages and political contexts. We introduce PolERo, a dataset of 3,574 human-annotated question-answer pairs extracted from official transcripts of five Romanian presidents. We evaluate multiple classification approaches on both datasets under matched conditions, including TF-IDF baselines, fine-tuned encoder models, a proposed sliding-window encoder, and zero/few-shot LLM prompting. We study cross-lingual transfer through joint bilingual training and machine-translation-based data augmentation. Our results indicate that fine-tuned encoders are competitive, cross-lingual transfer is asymmetric, and ambivalent evasion categories involving pragmatic cues remain the main challenge across all model families.

title: REPRESENTAÇÃO DO CONHECIMENTO NA INDÚSTRIA DO AUDIOVISUAL: MODELAGEM DE UMA ONTOLOGIA DE DOMÍNIO
abstract: As áreas de produção artística do audiovisual, como direção de arte, cenografia, figurino, caracterização e design gráfico, geram um grande volume de ativos digitais.Na ausência de modelos de representação do conhecimento, esses ativos têm sua reutilização dificultada e sua memória institucional comprometida.Objetivo: este artigo apresenta o processo de modelagem de uma ontologia voltada para a produção artística de conteúdos de dramaturgia para televisão.Originalidade/Valor: esta área envolve diversos processos de criação, produção e acervo, que produzem informações que precisam ser geridas e preservadas.A construção de uma ontologia neste domínio visa apoiar a organização e a representação do conhecimento na área, favorecendo a catalogação das informações, a interoperabilidade entre plataformas de produção e acervo e a aplicação de soluções baseadas em inteligência artificial.Metodologia: a pesquisa foi desenvolvida de acordo com a On-To-Knowledge Methodology (OTK), com base na ontologia de fundamentação de Sowa (2000) e apoiada por vocabulários de referência, como a MovieLabs Ontology for Media Creation, e na caracterização estrutural de processos de produção para televisão.Resultados: a ontologia desenvolvida foi implementada no software Protégé, sendo escalável para outros domínios da produção dramatúrgica com possibilidade de expansão para diferentes gêneros e formatos.Implicações Práticas: o trabalho contribui para um entendimento maior das especificidades de produção artística possibilitando, através da ontologia, ganho de produtividade, integração de sistemas de gestão do conhecimento e plataformas de produção, segurança da informação e potencial de inovação em gestão de ativos digitais neste setor.

title: The AUGMANITAI Concept Registry: A Public, Versioned, Author-Attributed Concept Registry — Reference Implementation of the Universal Concept Layer (v0.1)
abstract: Whitepaper on the AUGMANITAI Concept Registry — a public, versioned, author-attributed concept registry, live at augmanitai.com/registry/ as the reference implementation of the Universal Concept Layer (v0.1, bilingual English/German). Agent ecosystems are standardising transport, discovery and identity. The meaning level — what a term means, how its meaning changes over versions, and who coined it — has no public, versioned, cross-organisational infrastructure. This paper describes the design principles (terms as versioned artefacts with semantic versioning: MAJOR = break in meaning, MINOR = refinement, PATCH = wording; stable GET-addressable records; mandatory author attribution; evidence anchors per concept), the data model with schema, and the live reference implementation covering six signature concepts, each resolvable as JSON. title: 基于动态拓扑的概率模型构建
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology to probability modeling, proposing a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the underlying topology to simulate complex probability distributions. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static assumptions, limiting the model's ability to capture intricate phenomena. This work introduces a dynamic topology-based approach that allows for continuous parameter adjustment and emergent behavior, leading to more accurate probability predictions. We detail the core mechanism, including the construction of a probabilistic model based on dynamic topology, its implementation, and evaluation against established probabilistic methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for a wider range of applications.

title: A Large-Scale Sentiment Analysis of AI vs. Conventional Music Videos
abstract: Prior experimental research shows a robust AI-authorship bias, where consumers express lower appreciation for creative works when they are attributed to AI. Our analysis of music videos posted on YouTube Official Artist Channels (OAC) suggests a more nuanced pattern. We analyzed a corpus of more than 100 million comments left on over 4 million videos and found that comments posted on AI in Music (AIM) videos were, on average, more positive than comments left on conventional OAC videos. A notable exception was AI covers, where sentiment was significantly lower. Furthermore, although comments explicitly referencing AI were substantially less positive than those that did not, average sentiment towards AI remained nonetheless positive. Our findings suggest that audience resistance to AI music depends less on the mere presence of the technology, and more on whether AI is perceived as facilitating the creation of original music versus imitating or plagiarizing existing human works.

title: Formal Verification of Compiler Optimizations (FVCO)
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal verification techniques to compiler optimization algorithms. The core argument is that formal verification can provide guarantees regarding the correctness and efficiency of these optimizations. We treat compiler optimization algorithms as programs and utilize formal methods to validate their behavior, thereby mitigating potential errors introduced during the optimization process. This approach aims to enhance the reliability and trustworthiness of compiler optimizations, a critical area for ensuring software quality and performance. The paper details a framework for applying formal verification to compiler optimizations, focusing on key considerations and challenges. The overall goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating formal verification into the compiler design and analysis workflow.

title: Quantum Computing Genome Sequence Prediction
abstract: Quantum Computing Genome Sequence Prediction investigates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize gene sequencing analysis. Traditional methods face computational bottlenecks, hindering the accurate prediction of genetic sequences. This research explores the application of quantum algorithms to accelerate the prediction process, ultimately aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of gene sequence analysis. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum computation's unique properties to overcome limitations in classical algorithms and achieve superior prediction results. The investigation will detail a novel quantum approach to sequence prediction, focusing on reducing computational complexity and enhancing prediction fidelity. This paper will present a comprehensive overview of the proposed methodology, including mathematical formulations, key algorithmic steps, and potential performance benchmarks. The study will also address challenges related to quantum hardware limitations and the integration of existing bioinformatics tools.

title: Graph-Based Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Learning Models
abstract: Bayesian optimization is a powerful technique for hyperparameter tuning of deep learning models, offering efficiency compared to grid search or random search. However, its performance often degrades in high-dimensional hyperparameter spaces due to the "curse of dimensionality." This paper proposes a novel approach – Graph-Based Bayesian Optimization – that addresses this limitation by representing hyperparameters as nodes in a graph. The relationships between these nodes, captured through graph structure, are then leveraged to guide the optimization process, significantly improving exploration efficiency and reducing the computational cost associated with searching vast hyperparameter spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and present a conceptual framework. The core idea is to utilize graph theory to model the dependencies between hyperparameters, leading to a more focused and efficient search. This approach aims to overcome the challenges posed by high-dimensional spaces by exploiting inherent correlations, ultimately enabling faster convergence and better hyperparameter configurations for deep learning models. The efficiency gains stem from the ability to prioritize exploration based on graph connectivity and learned relationships, rather than blindly sampling points across the entire space.

title: Quantum Neural Networks with Dynamic Decoherence Suppression Mechanism
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the performance of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) through a dynamic decoherence suppression mechanism. Traditional decoherence mitigation strategies are often static and fail to adapt to the inherent fluctuations and noise present in quantum systems. We propose a feedback-based system that continuously monitors and corrects decoherence within the QNN, leveraging quantum measurement and control. The core claim of this work is to design a quantum feedback-based dynamic decoherence suppression mechanism to real-time monitor and correct decoherence in QNNs, thereby improving the network's computational capabilities and stability. The proposed mechanism relies on the core mechanism of utilizing quantum measurement and control to monitor and compensate for the decoherence effects, maintaining coherence between qubits. This dynamic approach addresses the limitations of static methods, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for QNNs. Mathematical formulations detailing the system dynamics and control strategies are presented, alongside a discussion of the theoretical underpinnings and potential applications. The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism is conceptually outlined, highlighting its ability to significantly improve the resilience of QNNs against environmental noise and ultimately boosting their computational performance. ---

title: Information Entropy-Driven Adaptive Neuron Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel neuron model driven by information entropy, termed the Information Entropy-Driven Adaptive Neuron Model (IEDANM). The core claim of this model is that the fundamental mechanism of neuronal information processing lies in entropy reduction. Neurons, through adaptive adjustments of their parameters, directly optimize for minimizing local entropy, thereby achieving efficient learning. The model utilizes information entropy as an intrinsic measure of neuronal state and employs gradient descent to optimize neuron parameters, maximizing the reduction in local entropy. This approach mirrors the self-organizing behavior observed in neurons during learning. The IEDANM offers a new perspective on neuronal learning mechanisms, originating from entropy theory and providing a novel framework for constructing neuronal models. The model's architecture and learning rules are defined to facilitate a biologically plausible simulation of neuronal adaptation. The key mathematical components include the definition of entropy, the gradient descent update rule, and the representation of neuronal parameters. This work aims to establish a theoretical foundation for understanding and simulating neuronal computation based on information theory principles. ---

title: Quantum Machine Learning: An Adaptive Loss Function Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning framework leveraging adaptive loss functions to enhance model generalization. Traditional loss functions often suffer from fixed parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. Our approach dynamically adjusts the loss function parameters, reducing computational cost and improving model performance through an intelligent mechanism. We detail the framework's design, explain its core mechanism, and discuss its potential impact on quantum machine learning.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Generator
abstract: This paper introduces a Dynamic Semantic Network Generator (DSNG), a novel system designed to automatically construct and maintain semantic networks representing complex, dynamic systems. The core of the DSNG is a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that adapts the network's structure and connections in response to changes in system states and external events. Unlike traditional static semantic networks, the DSNG allows for real-time semantic understanding and evolution, offering a more accurate and flexible representation of complex systems. The system utilizes a state representation, action space, and reward function to learn optimal network configurations. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging RL to continuously refine the network's topology and weights, mirroring the evolving relationships within the system under observation. This approach addresses the limitations of static models, providing a robust solution for analyzing and understanding systems where relationships are not fixed but constantly shifting. The system's performance is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its ability to capture and adapt to complex temporal dependencies.
